answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying vote and attestation weight to a vine of settled trades, not to a newly published name. Each increment is countersigned by counterparties and sealed under the agent's current cipher, which rotates every epoch so a stolen key cannot keep growing history. A comet of empty accounts inherits neither vine length nor cipher continuity; each clone must post a refundable lockup, wait, and complete real settlements before its voice counts. A thousand fakes then cost a thousand bonds and waiting periods, which honest agents have already paid once.
